# nestjs-error-registry

> Typed error catalog for NestJS. Define all your HTTP errors once with `errify()`, throw them with full TypeScript inference, get RFC 7807 Problem Details responses automatically, and have Swagger `@ApiResponse` schemas injected via `@Throws()` — without touching a single `@ApiResponse` decorator in your controllers.

## What it solves

NestJS applications scatter `throw new NotFoundException('...')` across services, throw generic strings as error messages, and require developers to manually maintain `@ApiResponse` decorators in controllers. There is no single source of truth for errors. `nestjs-error-registry` centralizes error definitions, enforces types at the call site, and wires Swagger + RFC 7807 automatically.

## Core API

### `errify(definitions)` — creates a typed error catalog

Each key maps to an `ErrorDefinition` with static metadata (`status`, `code`, `title`) and an optional dynamic message factory.

```ts
export const UserErrors = errify({
  NOT_FOUND: {
    status: 404,
    code: 'USR-404',
    title: 'User Not Found',
    message: (id: string) => `User with id ${id} not found`,
  },
  EMAIL_TAKEN: {
    status: 409,
    code: 'USR-409',
    title: 'Email Already Taken',
    message: 'Email already in use',
  },
});

// TypeScript infers (id: string) from the message factory:
throw UserErrors.NOT_FOUND(userId);

// TypeScript infers () for static messages:
throw UserErrors.EMAIL_TAKEN();
```

Returns an `ErrifyMap<T>` where each key is an `ErrifyFn` — a callable that throws `ErrifyError` and exposes `._meta` for `@Throws()` and Swagger.

### `ErrifyError`

Extends `HttpException`. Carries:
- `meta: ErrorMeta` — `{ status, code, title, messageTemplate }`
- `detail: string` — the resolved message (after calling the factory with args)
- `errorKey: string` — the catalog key (e.g. `'NOT_FOUND'`)

### `@Throws(...errorFns)` — method decorator

Applied to controller route handlers. Does two things:
1. Writes `ErrorMeta[]` to `Reflect` metadata under key `'errify:throws'` on the handler function — readable via `Reflector` in guards, interceptors, or tooling.
2. Injects `@ApiResponse` decorators for each declared error into the Swagger document, with an RFC 7807-compliant schema. Errors with the same HTTP status are grouped into a single `@ApiResponse` with a merged description and a `code` enum.

```ts
@Get(':id')
@Throws(UserErrors.NOT_FOUND, UserErrors.EMAIL_TAKEN)
async getUser(@Param('id') id: string) { ... }
```

`@nestjs/swagger` is an optional peer dependency — if not installed, `@Throws` skips Swagger injection silently.

### `ErrifyModule.forRoot(options?)` — root module

Registers `ErrifyExceptionFilter` as a global `APP_FILTER`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `string` | `''` | Prefix for the RFC 7807 `type` URI |
| `passthrough` | `boolean` | `true` | Forward non-ErrifyError HttpExceptions to default NestJS handling |

### `ErrifyExceptionFilter`

`@Catch()` filter that intercepts `ErrifyError` and returns RFC 7807 Problem Details:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/USR-404",
  "title": "User Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "User with id abc-123 not found",
  "instance": "/users/abc-123",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-07T20:00:00.000Z",
  "code": "USR-404"
}
```

Sets `Content-Type: application/problem+json`.

Non-ErrifyError exceptions are passed through when `passthrough: true` (default).

## RFC 7807 fields

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| `type` | `${baseUrl}/errors/${meta.code}` |
| `title` | `meta.title ?? meta.code` |
| `status` | `meta.status` |
| `detail` | Resolved message (factory result or static string) |
| `instance` | `request.url` |
| `timestamp` | `new Date().toISOString()` |
| `code` | `meta.code` — machine-readable, for programmatic error handling |

## TypeScript inference

The key type machinery in `src/types.ts`:

```ts
type InferArgs<T extends ErrorDefinition<any>> =
  T extends ErrorDefinition<infer A> ? A : [];

export type ErrifyMap<T extends Record<string, ErrorDefinition<any>>> = {
  readonly [K in keyof T]: ErrifyFn<InferArgs<T[K]>>;
};
```

`ErrorDefinition<A>` binds the tuple type `A` to the message factory's parameter list. `InferArgs` extracts it. The result is that each catalog key becomes a function whose parameter types are inferred directly from the `message` factory signature — no manual type annotations needed.

- [src/errify.ts](src/errify.ts) — `errify()` factory function
- [src/errify-error.ts](src/errify-error.ts) — `ErrifyError` class extending `HttpException`

- [src/errify.filter.ts](src/errify.filter.ts) — `ErrifyExceptionFilter`, RFC 7807 formatting
- [src/errify.module.ts](src/errify.module.ts) — `ErrifyModule.forRoot()`
